headline: Advance Online Entry and Camping Permits Required
reservation: Park entry fees are typically paid online in advance through the Sépaq portal to guarantee access, especially on peak weekends. Separate reservations are required for the park's yurts and campgrounds, which often book several months out. Verify the current season's entry requirements on the official Sépaq website.

days.title: Estuary Islands and Wildlife

stops.name: Cap-en-Ragis
stops.detail: Scan the shoreline for harbor seals and grey seals often seen hauling out on the rocks during low tide.

stops.name: Île aux Amours
stops.detail: Cross the tombolo during the low tide window to explore this small island within the estuary.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; slow speeds required within park boundaries.
days.note: Access to certain islands is strictly prohibited at high tide and during bird nesting periods.

days.title: Panoramic Ridges and Coastal Forests

stops.name: Pic Champlain
stops.detail: Ascend to the highest point in the park for a 346-meter vantage over the St. Lawrence River.

stops.name: Baie du Ha! Ha!
stops.detail: Explore the salt marshes and discover the unique flora that thrives in the brackish environment.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; park shuttle service may operate seasonally.
days.note: The shuttle schedule varies by month; verify current operation times at the visitor center.

days.title: Historic Capes and Coves

stops.name: Anse à l'Orignal
stops.detail: Walk the coastal path to see the distinctive geological formations of the Bas-Saint-Laurent region.

stops.name: Pointe-aux-Épinettes
stops.detail: Visit this peaceful cove for birdwatching, particularly during the spring and fall migration periods.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; watch for cyclists on the shared park roads.
days.note: Trails may be muddy following heavy rain; check trail status boards at the entrance.

intel.title: Tidal Crossing Safety
intel.text: The path to Île aux Amours is submerged twice daily. Check the official Sépaq tide clock at the trailhead before attempting the crossing.

intel.title: Valley Signal Shadows
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable near the park entrance but drops significantly in the coves and behind Pic Champlain. Rely on physical maps provided at the gate.

intel.title: Rimouski Hub
intel.text: No fuel is available inside the park. Fill your tank in Rimouski or the village of Le Bic before entering the park gates.

intel.title: Peak Season Crowds
intel.text: Summer weekends see the highest volume at the Pic Champlain lookout. Aim for early morning or late afternoon to secure a spot at the viewpoint.

intel.title: Trailhead Limitations
intel.text: Parking at Baie du Ha! Ha! is finite; during busy periods, staff may redirect visitors to the shuttle lots. Respect all no-parking signs to protect fragile roadside vegetation.

plan.arrival: Fly into Mont-Joli; collect supplies and groceries in Rimouski as village options in Le Bic are specialized and smaller.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for all paved park roads; RVs should check length restrictions for specific campgrounds.
plan.goldenHour: Pic Champlain is the premier location for sunset, offering a wide western horizon over the St. Lawrence estuary.
